text:
maya: Quick sync — I want to capture the experiment plan for integrating FA v2/v3 selector into the runtime. Short thread for decisions and action items
ryan: ok. main concerns: kernel switch cost, KV cache compatibility, and tail latency when we toggle.
sasha: agree. also need to avoid double-quantized kernels for the same model variant; that bit caused weird divergence last time.
maya: proposal: runtime exposes an `attn_selector` with 3 modes: `prefer_v3`, `prefer_v2`, `adaptive`. `adaptive` uses a lightweight probe and telemetry to pick per-request.
ryan: how lightweight? we need probe overhead << token cost. maybe 1-2 microbenchmarks per model load or per sequence length bucket.
sasha: we can sample 0.1% of requests and run a fast microbench that measures kernel latency at the current seq_len+kv_len. then increment counters for v2/v3 wins. after N samples update routing table.
eva: a few telemetry fields we should tag: `fa_version`, `seq_len_bucket`, `kv_cached_bytes`, `probe_result_ms`. ops: make sure these are gated by the `fa_selector_telemetry` flag for privacy/compliance.
ci-bot: deploy plan created: feature_flag=fa_selector_toggle, rollout=staged (10%->25%->50%->100%), monitor=latency_tokens,p50/p95/p99,model_fallbacks.
maya: good. specific KV cache compatibility notes: v3 uses paged attention memory alignment that increases per-kv-page eviction pressure on long-lived contexts. we should track `kv_evictions_per_min`. if evictions spike, throttle v3 routing.
ryan: add a fast heuristic: if `avg_kv_page_retention_time < threshold` then prefer v2 (less paged overhead). That avoids oscillation for chatty sessions.
sasha: batching heuristics — when we run hybrid batching across v2/v3, kernel switch means we can't batch requests from mixed selectors together. we should implement batch-aware routing: group by chosen kernel per-batch-window. does that hurt throughput? maybe small.
eva: perf profiling note: on the latest microbench, v3 win rate is strong for seq_len >= 1024 and KV < 64MB. v2 wins on low-seq short-prefill bursts. I'll attach numbers to the doc.
maya: for the rollout metrics, define automated guardrails: if p99_token_latency increases >15% vs baseline OR `model_error_rate` increases >0.2% rollback flag trips. Also require no spike in `cost_per_token` >12% for 24h at 50% rollout.
ryan: operational playbook for rollback: 1) flip feature_flag to `prefer_v2`, 2) drain ongoing sessions onto v2-friendly nodes, 3) run validation eval set (10k prompts) with both kernels, 4) escalate to eng-runtime on call if regressions persist.
sasha: can we add a short smoke check on deploy that runs this snippet?
sasha: ```
# smoke probe
python tools/probes/attn_probe.py --model my-model --seq 512 --kv 8M --iters 20
```
eva: nice. add `--warmup 2` to make sure caches are populated.
ops: telemetry retention: keep selector telemetry for 30 days by default and purge unless customer opts in. we'll surface per-customer opt-out.
maya: action items: ryan - implement selector flag + sampling probe (EOD Wed), sasha - batching grouping prototype (EOD Thu), eva - perf runs & telemetry schema (EOD Wed), ops - privacy gating & retention policy (EOD Fri).
ryan: I’ll push a PR with the flag scaffolding and a small YAML config example for thresholds.
sasha: ping @ryan for review when you push.
maya: perfect. we’ll reconvene after the first staged rollout (10%) to review p95/p99 and kv_eviction signals. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: created issue RF-4298 and linked this thread.
